required_outcomes: Reclassifies the issue from the content: this is a front door and frame fault (doors, windows, security), not an appliance; the fridge is mentioned only because the fridge installer witnessed the door problem.

Treats the front door as more than a routine job: it is the main entrance, so security and the risk of the glass shattering matter; raises the severity above ROUTINE or records why the timescale is tighter, and gives the tenant a safety note (avoid slamming; glass).
Requests landlord approval for the right trade (joiner, door and frame or lock specialist, not an appliance engineer), describing the door and frame fault.
Acknowledges the tenant and asks door-relevant questions (does it lock securely, is it glazed, is the back door the same) instead of the unanswered fridge questions.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the fridge contractor, who offered to report it, for his observations before writing to the landlord, as long as the landlord approval request is still raised promptly.
Sending someone to make the door safe under the security or emergency exemption if the door cannot be secured, with the landlord informed at once.
positive_behaviours: Notes that the back door has the same problem and asks whether both doors should be looked at.
Records the misclassification and the corrected category in the case notes.
Asks whether the property is currently secure (the door locks) to decide the urgency.
red_flags: Re-asks the appliance questions (fridge make and model, fridge or freezer affected).
Keeps the category as Appliances or sends an appliance engineer.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a maintenance provider before the landlord has approved, unless the door cannot be secured.
Closing or downgrading the request because the fridge questions were not answered.
critical_failures: Treating the request as a fridge or freezer fault and acting on that basis.
